summary: Iteration 7 — Tested (1) impersonation audit-log feature backend + UI, (2) stop-impersonation flow closing the log entry, (3) wallet/dashboard regression after _lookup_plan_and_price refactor, (4) sidebar duplicate-key warning fix. Backend: 12/12 impersonation tests pass, 18/18 wallet+dashboard regression tests pass. UI: impersonation-logs tab renders with all 7 Arabic columns, refresh button works, active-count badge shows '🟡 3 جلسة نشطة', stop-impersonation correctly POSTs /api/saas/impersonate/{sid}/stop BEFORE wiping localStorage, returns user to /saas-admin, and the audit-log entry transitions to status='closed' with duration_seconds=15. Bug fix for sidebar dedup is PARTIALLY effective: rendered DOM no longer contains duplicate hrefs for /wallet-management or /customers, but React STILL emits 'two children with the same key' warnings for these two paths on every tenant route navigation under impersonation context.

ui_bugs.issue: React duplicate-key console warning STILL fires for keys '/wallet-management' and '/customers' on every navigation, despite the Array.from(new Map(...)) dedupe and `${section.id || section.title}-${item.path}` key format on line 888-890. DOM verification shows only /defective-goods is actually duplicated in the rendered sidebar (1 dup of 77 links); /wallet-management and /customers appear once each — so the dedup IS visually working, but React's reconciliation is still detecting duplicate keys somewhere. Likely cause: the dedup runs inside the Link.map() but `customSidebarOrder` may build sections without unique section.id, OR a section's items array initially contains the dup BEFORE the user-defined order resolution (which Map would catch — so unlikely), OR the parent `<div key={section.title}>` is colliding because two distinct sections happen to share the same translated title — but the substituted warning value is the path string itself, indicating the inner Link key. Repro: log in as super_admin, impersonate any tenant, navigate among /, /wallet-management, /customers, /sales, /pos — 12 dup-key warnings collected in 5 nav hops.

action_items: Investigate why React duplicate-key warning still fires for /wallet-management and /customers despite Layout.js:888-890 fix. Suggestion: log the actual keys being generated by adding `console.log('key', `${section.id || section.title}-${item.path}`)` inside the .map(), navigate routes, and identify which two paths collide. Check customSidebarOrder branch (lines 600-672) for any path where item.path is duplicated WITHIN a single section's items array post-merge, and apply the same dedupe there. Alternatively, dedupe at the navSections-build level so that no single section.items array contains the same path twice.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 7: impersonation audit-log feature (backend + UI) is fully working end-to-end. The audit list, start, stop (incl. idempotency), filters, sort, auth gating, IP capture, session_id propagation to localStorage, AuthContext.stopImpersonation ordering — all verified live. Wallet/dashboard regression also clean (18/18). The ONLY outstanding issue is the React duplicate-key console warning for '/wallet-management' and '/customers' which still fires despite the Layout.js:888-890 dedup — the rendered DOM IS deduplicated correctly (only /defective-goods has a 2-DOM-instance dup, which existed before this iter). Main agent should add an extra dedup at navSections build time or stop trying to silence and accept that DOM-level dedup is sufficient (warning is dev-only). 3 active impersonation_logs rows left from intermediate test states; safe to ignore.
rca of the issue: Dup-key warning RCA: Layout.js renders Links via `<Link key={`${section.id || section.title}-${item.path}`}>`. DOM inspection shows /wallet-management and /customers each appear exactly once in the final rendered DOM (77 links, only /defective-goods duplicated). So the React fiber tree only contains ONE Link with key 'services-/wallet-management' and ONE with key 'saas-admin-/wallet-management' — these should be unique. Yet React's reconciliation logs the bare path '/wallet-management' (and '/customers') as the duplicate key. This strongly suggests there is ANOTHER .map() somewhere — perhaps inside a parent List wrapper (e.g., the `customSidebarOrder.filter(...).map(...)` chain in lines 611-655) — that uses item.path directly as a React child key on an intermediate React element. Need to grep for any JSX inside Layout.js or its imports that maps over a list containing path strings without explicit key prefixing.
